title: E: simple task won in 4 steps with an Anti-Pattern rule on screen
initial_observation:
-= Welcome to TextWorld, ALFRED! =-

You are in the middle of a room. Looking quickly around you, you see a bathtubbasin 1, a garbagecan 1, a handtowelholder 1, a shelf 3, a shelf 2, a shelf 1, a sinkbasin 1, a toilet 1, a toiletpaperhanger 1, and a towelholder 1.

Your task is to: put some candle on toilet.
plan: search the room for a candle
put the candle on the toilet

rules_shown.rule: When an object must be placed on a target: search the area first, open any closed containers, take the object, go to the target, move the object to the target.
rules_shown.example: search drawer 1, open drawer 1, take watch 1 from drawer 1, go to coffeetable 1, move watch 1 to coffeetable 1
rules_shown.validation: Confirmed: agent repeatedly examined desk without taking action, then took wrong object (pencil) instead of pen, and moved it to drawer instead of placing on surface. | Confirmed: object found on bed, target was desk, move command succeeded. | Confirmed: object found in closed drawer, required opening before taking, move command succeeded.
rules_shown.rendered_for_agent: [Success Process] When an object must be placed on a target: search the area first, open any closed containers, take the object, go to the target, move the object to the target. Example: search drawer 1, open drawer 1, take watch 1 from drawer 1, go to coffeetable 1, move watch 1 to coffeetable 1

rules_shown.rule: When examining an appliance, do not issue the same "examine" command again and again.
rules_shown.rendered_for_agent: [Anti-Pattern] When examining an appliance, do not issue the same "examine" command again and again. Example: "examine desk", again and again

rules_shown_to: planner (as the "rules" field of its prompt, before it writes subgoals) and actor (as the block "Rules learned from earlier practice (follow them)" in every step prompt); one set chosen once from the goal
shows: Two rules are shown: a Success Process and an Anti-Pattern ("When examining an appliance, do not issue the same examine command again and again"). The Anti-Pattern is irrelevant here (the agent never examines anything) but it is shown in every pick-and-place game.
why_interesting: Shows what an Anti-Pattern looks like in the prompt, and honestly shows its cost: it occupies prompt space in all 22 simple dev games although only a few agents loop on `examine`.

trace.observation: You arrive at shelf 1. On the shelf 1, you see a candle 1, a soapbar 2, and a soapbar 1.
You pick up the candle 1 from the shelf 1.
You arrive at toilet 1. On the toilet 1, you see a soapbottle 2.
You move the candle 1 to the toilet 1.
